verdict.rationale: Factory documents Droid Computers as dedicated execution machines where installed packages and running services persist between sessions. The Factory App also isolates each session in a separate working directory, and droid exec uses tiered autonomy to gate which operations need confirmation. However, nothing explicitly describes these environments as security-isolated sandboxes; worktree isolation is directory-level, not execution sandboxing. missing for 10: explicit sandbox/container isolation guarantees for code execution, documentation of safe dependency installation boundaries (network/filesystem restrictions), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent safely execute code and install dependencies inside an isolated sandbox

citations.quote: installed packages, files, running services, and configuration all persist between sessions
The Factory App creates a separate working directory for the session, prepares it, and keeps it isolated from your other work.
Droid exec uses tiered autonomy to control what operations can run without manual confirmation.
